coreLogic: The entire body of Format::file_size is the core logic: a non-numeric guard (`if(!is_numeric($bytes)) return $bytes;`) followed by three branches — bytes (`$bytes < 1024` -> "{$bytes} bytes"), kb (`$bytes < (900<<10)` i.e. 921600 -> `round($bytes/1024,1)` . ' kb'), and mb (else -> `round($bytes/1048576,1)` . ' mb'). No other function is called from within file_size; it is a single self-contained calculation with no delegation chain to follow.

inputShape: Single positional argument $bytes: expected to be an int or a numeric string representing a byte count (e.g. attachment File->size, or a computed power-of-two limit like `512 << 10`). Value is passed through PHP's is_numeric() check first, so it may arrive as int, float, or numeric string; non-numeric values (e.g. null coerced to '', or an arbitrary string) are explicitly supported as a passthrough case.
outputShape: String. Either the original $bytes value unchanged (non-numeric passthrough, no unit suffix appended) or a formatted string in one of three shapes: '<int> bytes' (no rounding, exact byte count), '<float, 1 decimal> kb' (bytes/1024 rounded to 1 decimal), or '<float, 1 decimal> mb' (bytes/1048576 rounded to 1 decimal). No HTML escaping or localization is applied inside file_size itself.
sideEffects: None. file_size() is a pure static function: no database reads/writes, no reads of $cfg or other globals, no session/cache access, no file I/O, no mutation of its argument, and it calls no other methods or functions internally.
constraints: Non-numeric input must return $bytes unchanged (exact object/value passthrough, not a stringified or reformatted version) — this must be checked and returned before any arithmetic is attempted
The bytes-vs-kb threshold is a strict '<' at 1024 (i.e. 1023 -> 'bytes', 1024 -> 'kb'), not '<='
The kb-vs-mb threshold is a strict '<' at (900<<10) = 921600 bytes, not a round 1024*1024 boundary — this literal value must be preserved exactly, not simplified to 900*1024 or replaced with 1048576
kb and mb branches must round to exactly 1 decimal place using PHP round($x, 1) semantics (not floor/ceil, not a different precision)
The bytes branch must not apply round() or any decimal formatting — it concatenates the raw numeric value with ' bytes'
Unit suffix strings must remain exactly ' bytes', ' kb', ' mb' (lowercase, with leading space) since callers embed the returned string directly into HTML/UI text with no further transformation
Method must remain a static entry point on Format with the identical signature `file_size($bytes)` so all 10 existing call sites keep working without changes
No caller-visible behavior change is permitted for any of the boundary cases (0, 1023, 1024, non-numeric, just under/over 921600, large mb values) after delegating to the extracted service
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field 'bytes' (mixed: int, numeric string, or non-numeric string) representing the raw byte count to pass into Format::file_size(). The harness should pass this value through unmodified (preserving its original PHP type where JSON allows) so both numeric and non-numeric-string test cases can be captured, e.g. {"bytes": 0}, {"bytes": 1023}, {"bytes": 1024}, {"bytes": "unknown"}, {"bytes": 921599}, {"bytes": 921600}, {"bytes": 5242880}.
